children: The recent gains in shares of Home Depot

represent an outsized lift from “siren-song” assumptions that homeowners’ finances will remain historically strong and that the two leading home improvement retailers’ category positions are untouchable.
Said differently, the bull case for Home Depot and Lowe’s assumes that homeowners will stay financially healthy and the two will remain dominant in the space.
Unfortunately, Stifel analyst W. Andrew Carter warns that while those assumptions are tempting, they are also risky, especially how they pertain to Lowe’s

given its overexposure to the challenges of operating margin pressure, structural issues that include known do-it-yourself weakness, housing category uncertainty, and increased competition requiring investments to sustain long-term growth prospects, with the latter putting additional pressure on Lowe’s

Accordingly, Carter believes LOW shares will remain under pressure as these challenges are fully digested starting with third-quarter results and next month’s Investor Day, leading the analyst to downgrade LOW to Sell from Hold.

to report results next week (Home Depot on Nov. 17, Lowe's on Nov. 18), Carter expects their results will reflect a weaker market within the home improvement category “at best stable with uneven October commentary.”

“We believe Lowe’s specialty trade performance will meaningfully trail expectations given higher new residential construction exposure…and the change in homebuilder expectations suggests an over 70 basis point headwind to its fourth quarter comparable sales,” Carter writes.

Carter’s margin outlook for FY27 to FY28 also underscores his caution in the space. He estimates operating margin for both will be compressed by 28 basis points for Home Depot and by 20 basis points for Lowe’s compared to the consensus estimates for expansion of 36 basis points and 34 basis points, respectively, given supply chain inflation and manufacturer price increases.
“We believe turnover reaching levels to meaningfully accelerate category growth will be difficult with affordability issues constraining turnover and project spending power,” Carter adds.
third-quarter results are expected to show the retailer earned a profit of $2.88 per share on $22.36B in sales, a change of -6% and +7% from last year, respectively.
